title: Massachusetts Seller Property Condition Statement
description: Massachusetts does not have a comprehensive mandatory seller disclosure statute comparable to many other states. However, sellers must disclose known material defects and may not actively conceal defects. The standard practice is to use a voluntary seller's statement of property condition. Massachusetts courts impose liability for fraudulent concealment of known defects.

required_actions.note: No comprehensive statutory disclosure form required, but sellers must not conceal known material defects. Standard practice to use MAR seller's statement of property condition.

citations: Swinton v. Whitinsville Sav. Bank, 311 Mass. 677 (1942)

title: Agency Disclosure — Mandatory Written Consent for Dual Agency
description: Massachusetts 254 CMR 3.00 requires licensees to disclose their agency relationship in writing at the first personal meeting. Massachusetts prohibits undisclosed dual agency; dual agency is permitted only with advance informed written consent of all parties. Failure to disclose dual agency is grounds for license revocation under MGL c.112 §87AAA.

required_actions.note: Dual agency REQUIRES advance written consent from ALL parties. Undisclosed dual agency is prohibited and is grounds for license action.

title: Mandatory Lead Paint Inspection (Pre-1978) — Massachusetts Enhanced
description: MGL c.111 §197 requires a lead paint inspection for all residential properties built before 1978 when a child under 6 resides there. Massachusetts lead paint law is among the strictest in the nation. The seller must disclose all known lead paint conditions and provide a lead paint inspection report (if one exists). Buyers of pre-1978 homes should be advised to obtain a lead inspection. Deleading may be required.

required_actions.note: Disclose all known lead paint inspection reports. If child under 6 will reside, inspection/deleading may be required under MGL c.111 §197.

title: Closing Type — Attorney State
description: Massachusetts is an attorney state for real estate closings. The practice of closing real estate transactions, including title examination, document preparation, and conducting the settlement, is considered the practice of law. Both buyer and seller typically retain separate attorneys.

required_actions.note: Massachusetts requires attorney involvement for closing. Title examination, document preparation, and settlement are the practice of law. Both parties typically retain separate counsel.

citations: SJC Rule 3:07 (Unauthorized Practice of Law Guidelines)

title: Smoke and Carbon Monoxide Detector Compliance Certificate
description: MGL c.148 §26F½ requires sellers to obtain a certificate of compliance for smoke detectors and carbon monoxide detectors from the local fire department before the sale can close. The certificate must be provided to the buyer at or before closing.

required_actions.note: Seller must contact local fire department for inspection and obtain certificate of compliance before closing.
